definition: An Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS Region.
A zonal shift temporarily moves a supported resource traffic away from one Availability Zone.
Zonal autoshift authorizes AWS to move configured resource traffic when AWS telemetry detects a potential zonal impairment.
A practice run tests whether an application can operate with resource traffic shifted away from one zone.
Prescaling provisions enough capacity before a zonal shift to serve traffic without one zone.
Telemetry is measurement data AWS uses to detect a potential zonal impairment.
An administrative override records deliberate target exclusion separately from target health.
Fail open is a load balancer state in which lack of healthy targets prevents zonal shift from moving traffic away.
An application replica is a deployment that can serve the workload in another zone or Region.
A cluster endpoint is a regional API address used to read or update routing control states.
A control panel groups related routing controls so they can share safety rules.
An assertion rule rejects a routing control update when its required state conditions would be violated.
A gating rule uses a master control to allow or block changes to target routing controls.
The routing control data plane reads and updates the live routing control states used for failover.
The routing control configuration control plane creates or deletes clusters, panels, and routing controls.
DNS resolves application names into addresses that clients can connect to.
TTL specifies how long a DNS answer can be cached before it must be refreshed.
An ARN is the AWS identifier for a routing control or another resource.
A readiness check audits application replicas for capacity and configuration differences that could affect failover.
